He could, though not far, and not against the current that came around the point after three o'clock. The shop had closed years before. The church opened twice a summer when the priest came over from the mainland with a thermos and a hymnbook and a look of gentle apology, as though the emptiness were his fault. Einar attended both services. He did not believe much, but he liked the sound of another voice in the rafters, and he liked that the priest never asked why he stayed.

She wrote about her children and their schools and the price of things in Trondheim. He read each letter twice, once for the news and once for her handwriting, which had not changed since she was twelve.

What he did not write back was that the island had grown honest with him. The tide did not pretend. The rocks did not soften. The cormorants on the skerry dried their wings and paid him no attention at all, and he found in that a kind of respect.
